belief: Wealth proves God is pleased with me.
origins: When things go well, it is natural to give thanks. The danger is concluding that success is God’s stamp of approval. Teaching that links faithfulness with financial reward can lead us to read our bank balance as a spiritual report card, and to look down on those who have less.
teaches: Jesus said, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.” Paul tells the rich not to be conceited or to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God. Proverbs warns that he who trusts in his riches will fall. Jesus said it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. Wealth can be a gift, but it is not a sign of God’s favor.
self_statements: God is blessing me because I am doing right.
My success shows I am in His favor.
People who struggle must be doing something wrong.
If I lose this, God must be displeased.
errors: Believing that people always get what they deserve.
Feeling blessed and concluding that wealth means approval.
Seeing wealth as proof and poverty as failure.
questions: Where did I learn that wealth means God’s approval?
Do I know people who are faithful and not wealthy, or wealthy and not faithful?
How did Jesus and the apostles live?
What does Jesus say about trusting in riches?
What would I conclude about God’s pleasure if I lost my money?
How can I hold wealth with thanks and openness?
truth: God is pleased with me because of Christ, not because of my balance. Wealth is a gift to steward and share, not a measure of His approval. I can give thanks without judging myself or others by money.
hw_truths: God’s approval does not come from wealth.
My hope is in God, not riches.
Wealth is a gift to share.
Others’ struggles are not proof of their failure.
I am pleasing to Him in Christ.
log: Each week, write one thing you have and how you can share or steward it.
actions: Write where you learned that wealth equals blessing.
Name ten gifts from God that are not financial.
Give time, money, or help to someone this week.
Ask God to keep your hope in Him.
prayer: Father, thank You for what You have given me. Keep me from reading my wealth as Your approval. Help me trust You, share generously, and love people regardless of what they have. Amen.
hw_questions: Where did I learn wealth means approval?
What non-money blessings do I have?
How do I view people with less?
What if I lost it all?
name_example: Sarah can write: “My life does not consist of my possessions, so wealth is not proof of God’s favor.”
